log_events_added.severity: UNDECLARED — plan cites the call (v4 §B.4 step 13.5, §B.6) but never declares severity level
log_events_added.label_keys: UNDECLARED — ticket carries account_id, provider_family, model_hint; none are named as structured log keys
log_events_added.conformance_gap: The function `emit_audit_event` is invented in the plan. ADR-0003 defines the authoritative AuditEvent struct with mandatory fields: event_id (ULID), tenant_shard (TenantId), prior_block_hash (BlockHash), event_class (EventClass), principal (PrincipalRef), capability (Option<CapabilityId>), data_classes_touched (BTreeSet<DataClass>), regulatory_packs_consumed (BTreeSet<RegulatoryPackId>), autonomy_tier_at_decision (Option<AutonomyTier>), payload (AuditPayload), timestamp_utc. None of these fields are declared in the plan's `emit_audit_event` call. The plan cites `existing evidence + run + step (ADR-0003)` in the change context but does not show how UsageBlocked maps to the chain schema.

This is declared as a TEST ASSERTION (tests/audit_chain.rs) — on-call cannot query it at 3am. C.8 asserts 'every spawn/commit emits EvidenceRef linked to capability_id' but does not declare the event as a production structured log. No severity, no additional label keys (account_id, provider_family, message_id, tick_epoch_secs, tokens_in, tokens_out), no transport (OTLP? JSONL? ClickHouse?). The plan never declares whether EvidenceRef conforms to AuditEvent (ADR-0003) or is a separate bespoke type.

log_events_omitted.why_needed: On-call needs to see each message dispatch: which message_id, which account, which provider, which tier. Without this, a processing stall is invisible in logs.
TickOutcome::Saturated means all permits consumed; if this fires continuously, inbox grows without bound. No log = no 3am signal.
Idle outcome is normal, but sustained idle when inbox is non-empty indicates a lock-TTL or peek_lock bug. Only diagnosable if inbox_depth is also logged.
TickOutcome::Quarantined(MessageId) is a terminal bad-message event. Should fire at ERROR with the message_id hash and reason.
Watchdog SIGTERM is declared (v4 §B.3) but no log event is declared. Repeated watchdog kills = runaway driver. On-call cannot observe this pattern.
SIGKILL follows SIGTERM after 1s timeout. Escalation path must be separately observable.
ProviderAccount::degrade() is called in tick_once steps 9 (OverUsageLimit, ReserveBreached). No log event declared. Account quietly leaves rotation with no trace.

InboxStore::dead_letter() (atomic, v4 patch #6) is called for both cost-ceiling exceeded and poison-message paths. The log event is conflated with emit_audit_event for the ceiling case only; the poison-message path has no declared log event.
Window rotation (step 9, WindowExpired) is a conditional recursive path in tick_once. No log event declared. If rotation loops, there is no observable signal.
RoutePolicy::select outcome (including RouteExplanation.reason) is not logged. Without this, on-call cannot tell which account won routing and why.
When AccountSnapshotProvider excludes an account due to drift (VerifyMode::FailOnDrift, v5 §B.4), no structured log is declared. On-call sees fewer eligible accounts with no explanation.

metrics_added.label_set: UNDECLARED — plan cites the name (v4 §A.4 scenario c) but declares no label keys
metrics_added.plan_reference: v4 §A.4 scenario (c) poison message loop mitigation
metrics_added.gap: No label keys declared. Recommended label set: {reason_category: enum(parse_failed, max_retries_exceeded), provider_family: enum(Claude|OpenAiOrCodex|Gemini|Aws)}. Missing: the plan does not declare where or how this counter is registered (tracing? OTel Meter? InMemoryMetrics?). Without registration declaration, this metric may not survive Branch Y dependency constraints.

metrics_added.type: JSONL bench artifact — NOT a runtime OTel metric
metrics_added.gap: This is a bench harness artifact emitted to disk at test time ({metric: idle_tick_p95_tokens, value: <n>, p: 95}). It is NOT a production metric instrument. On-call cannot query it in VictoriaMetrics at 3am. The plan conflates bench perf budgets with runtime observability.

metrics_added.type: JSONL bench artifact — NOT a runtime OTel metric
metrics_added.gap: Same as idle_tick_p95_tokens — bench artifact, not production instrument.

metrics_added.type: JSONL bench artifact — NOT a runtime OTel metric
metrics_added.gap: Same. Additionally: /proc/self/status VmRSS is Linux-only; plan correctly gates to cfg(target_os=linux) but the equivalent production RSS metric (for capacity planning) is also absent.

metrics_added.type: JSONL bench artifact — NOT a runtime OTel metric
metrics_added.gap: Same bench-artifact conflation. The production equivalent (runtime counter of actual watchdog kills) is absent.

metrics_omitted.why_needed: Primary health signal for the supervisor. Without this, 3am on-call cannot determine spawn rate or failure distribution.
TickOutcome::Saturated fires when in_flight_permits == max_in_flight. Without this gauge, on-call cannot distinguish 'no messages' from 'all slots full'. Critical for capacity planning.

Unprocessed message backlog. Non-zero + Saturated = normal. Non-zero + not Saturated for >N ticks = pathological. The dashboard-kernel projection rows reference 'inbox_depth' (per change context) but neither v4 nor v5 plan declares how this is populated or how it surfaces as a runtime metric.

Dead-lettered messages are terminal failures. Separate from quarantine_total (quarantine is a verdict path; dead-letter is the storage outcome). On-call needs to distinguish cost-ceiling kills from parse failures.

tick_once runs steps 1-17 including I/O, subprocess spawn, and billing API calls. Without a histogram, 3am cannot distinguish 'tick is slow' from 'tick is failing fast'. Pairs with supervisor_spawn_total to compute per-outcome latency.
Watchdog fires are declared in §B.3 but no runtime counter exists. A SIGKILL storm (driver bug, filesystem hang) is invisible in production.
Accounts degrade silently in steps 9 and 11. Without a counter, the on-call cannot tell if all Claude accounts have degraded overnight.
v5 §B.4 semantics extension: drifting accounts are excluded from snapshot. Without a counter, on-call cannot tell if drift-exclusion is reducing the account pool.

spans_omitted.why_needed: tick_once is the critical path spanning steps 1-17: JSONL lock, account snapshot (+ v5 drift verify), route selection, usage enforcement, projection check, ceiling check, driver spawn, stdout drain, billing validate, commit, outbox append. No span boundary means zero trace visibility. If step 7 hangs (usage window I/O), on-call sees only a silent stall.

This is a fork+exec of an external CLI process. It is the highest-latency, highest-risk operation in the system. ADR-0042 requires gen_ai semantic conventions per capability invocation: gen_ai.system, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, oya.foundry.capability, oya.tenant.id. None are declared.

POST /v1/supervisor/inbox is the ingest surface. While TelemetryMiddleware covers route/method/status_class at the HTTP layer (existing infra), no span wraps the full handler execution including inbox.peek_lock + JSONL write. On-call cannot distinguish 'slow ingest' from 'slow inbox write'.
peek_lock acquires a 30s TTL lock from JSONL. If filesystem is slow or file is corrupt, this call hangs. No span = no trace entry for the hang.
SettingsRenderer::render writes to ~/.claude/, ~/.codex/, ~/.gemini/. File I/O operations under ~ can be slow (NFS, quota exceeded, permissions). No span declared.
SettingsRenderer::verify runs at every AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot() call (step 2 of tick_once in v5). If verify is slow, it blocks the entire tick_once path. No span.

dashboard_kernel_projection_gap.claim_in_change_context: New dashboard-kernel projection rows: session, inbox_depth, outbox_tail, idle_ticks_total
dashboard_kernel_projection_gap.gap_analysis: The task message asserts four new projection rows as a fact of this change. None appear in v4 or v5 plan artifacts. No InboxDepthView, OutboxTailView, or IdleTicksView is declared. No integration path from tick_once outcomes → dashboard-kernel is specified. The existing SessionView is for ProviderAccount auth-sessions (started_at/expires_at/privacy_boundary), NOT for supervisor message-processing sessions. If dashboard-kernel projections are intended, they require: (a) new view structs in oya-foundry-dashboard-kernel, (b) a write adapter that calls tick_once and projects results, (c) grit claim units. None are present. This is either a spec gap (the change does not actually add these rows) or a plan omission (BLOCKER-level).

http_telemetry_wiring_gap.existing_infra: oya-http-telemetry-middleware-infrastructure::TelemetryMiddleware covers route/method/status_class/latency for any MiddlewareChain consumer
http_telemetry_wiring_gap.plan_reference: v4 §B.7 — Router<SyncHandler> + MiddlewareChain + serve() — no TelemetryMiddleware in the composition
http_telemetry_wiring_gap.gap_analysis: The supervisor HTTP surface (POST /v1/supervisor/inbox, GET /v1/supervisor/health, GET /v1/supervisor/outbox/{seq}) is mounted via oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter::serve(addr, Arc::new(router), Arc::new(chain), ServerConfig). The MiddlewareChain is constructed but the plan does not declare TelemetryMiddleware in the chain. If it is not explicitly wired, the three HTTP routes will have zero per-route metrics in VictoriaMetrics. This is not automatic.

pii_cardinality_risks.risk: HIGH — If used as a metric label, cardinality = number of distinct accounts. Plan shows multi-account fanout as a core feature (N accounts × 3 providers). Should be hashed or replaced with a stable low-cardinality alias (e.g., provider_family + account_index). Plan makes no cardinality declaration.
HIGH — Free-form string in SessionTicket. If used as a metric label, cardinality is unbounded (any string accepted). Plan declares no cardinality ceiling.

pii_cardinality_risks.field: reason: String in DeadLettered { reason } and Released { reason }
pii_cardinality_risks.risk: MEDIUM — Free-form reason string in InboxState enum variants. If logged directly as a label key value, could contain sensitive message content or user data. Plan declares no sanitization contract.

MEDIUM — If used as a trace or log label, each unique message = unique cardinality value. Acceptable in trace span attributes but must not be a metric label. Plan does not segregate trace-attribute fields from metric-label fields.
LOW — v5 §C.29 correctly gates raw secret exposure via grep test. SettingsRenderer::render writes env-var names only, not resolved values. C.29 acceptance row covers this. Credit given.

diagnosability_walkthrough:
Failure scenario: supervisor processes zero messages for 30 minutes at 3am. Provider: Claude. Error mode: tick_once is returning Idle despite a non-empty inbox. On-call tries to diagnose from logs + metrics + traces.

[LOGS]: No structured log event is declared for TickOutcome::Idle or TickOutcome::Saturated. The only named log call in the plan is emit_audit_event('UsageBlocked', &ticket) — which fires on cost-ceiling exceeded, not on Idle. On-call will see silence in ClickHouse for the supervisor.tick_once.* event namespace. There is no log entry showing 'tick fired, inbox had N messages, result was Idle'. On-call cannot confirm the supervisor is even running its tick loop without SSH access to the host.

[METRICS]: supervisor_quarantine_total exists (if registered — plan does not declare the registration point). It would be zero in the Idle scenario. supervisor_in_flight_gauge does not exist, so on-call cannot confirm whether the semaphore is full (Saturated) vs. the inbox is empty (true Idle). supervisor_inbox_depth_gauge does not exist, so on-call cannot see the unprocessed backlog. The 4 bench JSONL metrics (idle_tick_p95_tokens etc.) are not queryable in VictoriaMetrics — they are test harness artifacts. HTTP route metrics MAY exist if TelemetryMiddleware was wired (not declared), showing whether POST /v1/supervisor/inbox is receiving requests. On-call can infer whether messages are arriving but not whether the tick loop is consuming them.

[TRACES]: Zero spans declared. Jaeger/Tempo shows nothing for this supervisor. On-call cannot see which step in tick_once (steps 1-17) is hanging. If peek_lock is returning None due to a TTL bug (all messages locked by a crashed-but-unreleased reservation), there is no span showing the lock-acquisition attempt and its None result.

[AUDIT CHAIN]: EvidenceRef is declared as a test assertion (tests/audit_chain.rs asserts spawn/commit emit it). In production, if the audit chain is wired, on-call could query for the last EvidenceRef timestamp and infer when the last successful spawn occurred. However, the plan does not declare the audit chain as a 3am diagnostic tool — it is declared as a regulatory compliance artifact. The query surface (ClickHouse? trust portal?) and the event schema conformance (AuditEvent per ADR-0003 vs bespoke EvidenceRef) are both unspecified.

[CONCLUSION]: This supervisor is not diagnosable from logs+metrics+traces alone at 3am. On-call would need SSH access to the host, manual inspection of inbox/*.jsonl files, and manual reading of dead-letter/ directories. The gap is architectural: the plan treats observability as a test-gate concern (audit_chain.rs, bench JSONL) rather than a production runtime concern (structured logs with severity + OTel spans + metric instruments registered at app startup).

findings.title: Zero structured log events declared for tick_once lifecycle outcomes
findings.description: The plan declares four TickOutcome variants (Spawned, Saturated, Idle, Quarantined) but emits no structured log event for any of them. On-call cannot determine from logs why the supervisor is in any given state. ADR-0042 requires per-event tenant + cell + axis + capability tags; none are declared.
findings.evidence: v4 §B.2.5 declares TickOutcome enum; no corresponding tracing::info!/warn!/error! calls in §B.4 call chain steps 1-17; v4 §A.5 test table has 'Observability' row pointing only to audit_chain.rs test, not production emission.
findings.remediation: Declare at minimum: tracing::info!(outcome=%outcome, provider_family=%pf, message_id_hash=%hash, 'supervisor.tick_once') after each tick_once resolution. Add severity escalation: Quarantined → ERROR, Saturated sustained N ticks → WARN.

findings.title: emit_audit_event does not conform to ADR-0003 AuditEvent schema
findings.description: v4 §B.4 step 13.5 calls emit_audit_event('UsageBlocked', &ticket). ADR-0003 defines AuditEvent with mandatory fields: event_id (ULID), tenant_shard (TenantId), prior_block_hash (BlockHash), event_class (EventClass), principal (PrincipalRef), capability (Option<CapabilityId>), data_classes_touched (BTreeSet<DataClass>), regulatory_packs_consumed (BTreeSet<RegulatoryPackId>), autonomy_tier_at_decision (Option<AutonomyTier>), payload (AuditPayload), timestamp_utc. The plan's call signature passes only a string literal and a SessionTicket — it cannot satisfy the chain schema without a wrapper that is neither declared nor grit-claimed.
findings.evidence: ADR-0003 AuditEvent struct (crates/oya-audit-chain-kernel); v4 §B.4 step 13.5 'emit_audit_event("UsageBlocked", &ticket)'; zero grit units in §B.12 claim any audit-chain-kernel integration crate or wrapper.
findings.remediation: Declare an `emit_supervisor_audit_event` function in supervisor-app that constructs a conformant AuditEvent (event_class: EventClass::CapabilityInvocation or a new EventClass::UsageBlocked, capability: foundry.supervisor.dead_letter capability_id from §B.8, autonomy_tier_at_decision: from ticket.autonomy_tier). Add a grit unit for this function. Add a test asserting the constructed event passes ADR-0003 chain schema validation.

findings.title: Zero spans declared — tick_once and driver spawn are dark to the trace store
findings.description: The plan introduces a complex 17-step critical path (tick_once) and an external process spawn (driver.spawn_for_message). Neither has a declared OTel span. ADR-0042 mandates OTLP/gRPC trace export with gen_ai semantic conventions per capability invocation: gen_ai.system, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, oya.foundry.capability, oya.tenant.id. None are declared. Jaeger shows nothing for this supervisor at 3am.
findings.evidence: v4 §B.4 call chain steps 1-17 — no tracing::Span, no #[tracing::instrument]; ADR-0042 §Per-capability gen_ai semantic conventions table; v4 §B.0 workspace deps confirm 'tracing' is present (Cargo.toml:481-492) but no span API usage is declared anywhere in the plan.
findings.remediation: Declare at minimum: (1) tracing::span!(Level::INFO, 'supervisor.tick_once', outcome=tracing::field::Empty) wrapping the full tick_once body; (2) tracing::span!(Level::INFO, 'supervisor.driver.spawn', gen_ai.system=%system, gen_ai.request.model=%model_hint, oya.foundry.capability=%cap_id) wrapping driver.spawn_for_message. Add these span declarations as grit units.

findings.title: Four bench JSONL metrics conflated with production runtime metrics
findings.description: The plan presents idle_tick_p95_tokens, restart_latency_p95_ms, rss_max_kib, watchdog_kill_p95_ms (C.13a-d) as the supervisor's metric story. These are bench harness output rows written to a JSONL file at test time. They are not OTel metric instruments registered in a Meter and exported to VictoriaMetrics. On-call cannot query them at 3am. The only explicitly named production metric is supervisor_quarantine_total — itself missing label keys and registration point.
findings.evidence: v4 §A.5 bench row: 'emits one JSONL row per metric per the schema declared in §C.13'; v4 §C.13a-d: JSONL row schema {metric: ..., value: ..., p: 95}; ADR-0042: 'Metrics. OTLP/HTTP export; OpenMetrics-compatible'; no Meter registration, no opentelemetry::metrics::Counter/Gauge/Histogram declarations anywhere in the plan.
findings.remediation: Define a SupervisorMetrics struct in supervisor-app holding: spawn_total (Counter), in_flight_gauge (ObservableGauge), inbox_depth_gauge (ObservableGauge), dead_letter_total (Counter), watchdog_kill_total (Counter), tick_duration (Histogram). Register via OTel Meter at app startup. Keep bench JSONL for perf-budget CI gates but stop treating them as the observability story.

findings.title: Dashboard-kernel projection rows (inbox_depth, outbox_tail, idle_ticks_total) referenced in change context but absent from plan
findings.description: The change_class context asserts 'New dashboard-kernel projection rows (session, inbox_depth, outbox_tail, idle_ticks_total)'. Reading crates/oya-foundry-dashboard-kernel/src/lib.rs confirms existing views are AccountHealthView, SessionView (auth-sessions), UsageView, RoutingView. None of the supervisor-specific rows appear. The v4 plan does not declare InboxDepthView, OutboxTailView, or IdleTicksView, and has zero grit units for dashboard-kernel changes.
findings.evidence: crates/oya-foundry-dashboard-kernel/src/lib.rs — full file read, no supervisor-specific views present; v4 §B.12 — 49 grit units, none target oya-foundry-dashboard-kernel; v4 §B.0 surfaces inventory — dashboard-kernel not listed as a composed surface.
findings.remediation: Either (a) remove the dashboard-kernel claim from the change context if these rows are out of scope for v4+v5, or (b) add an explicit §B-dashboard section declaring InboxDepthView, OutboxTailView, IdleTicksView types, the write path from tick_once, and corresponding grit units. The projection structs must follow ReadOnlyProjection marker pattern (no &mut self, existing invariant).

findings.title: TelemetryMiddleware wiring not declared for supervisor HTTP surface
findings.description: oya-http-telemetry-middleware-infrastructure::TelemetryMiddleware is the existing per-route metrics infra (route, method, status_class, latency_us). The supervisor HTTP routes (POST /v1/supervisor/inbox, GET /v1/supervisor/health, GET /v1/supervisor/outbox/{seq}) are mounted via oya-http-runtime-hyper-adapter::serve(addr, Arc::new(router), Arc::new(chain), ServerConfig). The plan does not declare TelemetryMiddleware in the MiddlewareChain construction. Without explicit wiring, the three HTTP routes will have zero per-route metrics in production.
findings.evidence: v4 §B.7: 'let router = Router::<SyncHandler>::new().route(...)' + 'oya_http_runtime_hyper_adapter::serve(addr, Arc::new(router), Arc::new(chain), ...)' — chain construction not shown, TelemetryMiddleware not mentioned; crates/oya-http-telemetry-middleware-infrastructure/src/lib.rs confirmed to exist and work correctly.
findings.remediation: Add explicit TelemetryMiddleware wiring to §B.7: 'let metrics = Arc::new(InMemoryMetrics::new()); let chain = MiddlewareChain::new().push(Box::new(TelemetryMiddleware::new(metrics.clone()))); oya_http_runtime_hyper_adapter::serve(addr, Arc::new(router), Arc::new(chain), ServerConfig::default()...)'. Add grit unit for this wiring.

findings.title: InboxState transitions not instrumented — stuck states are invisible
findings.description: The 7-variant InboxState machine (Queued/Locked/InFlight/DraftedResponse/Committed/DeadLettered/Released) has zero declared observability. If messages accumulate in Locked state due to expired TTLs not being GC'd, or stick in DraftedResponse because outbox.append fails, on-call has no observable signal. next_inbox_state transitions are pure functions (correct) but emit nothing observable.
findings.evidence: v4 §B.2.1 InboxState enum; v4 §B.2.2 next_inbox_state pure fn; v4 §B.3 state machine table — no log/metric emission declared at any transition.
findings.remediation: Emit a tracing::event at each terminal state transition (Committed, DeadLettered, Released) from the supervisor-app layer (not the kernel — kernel is I/O-free). Add supervisor_inbox_state_total counter with label {terminal_state: enum(committed|dead_lettered|released)} to track message throughput and failure rates.

findings.title: gen_ai semantic conventions not declared for any capability invocation
findings.description: ADR-0042 mandates gen_ai semantic conventions per capability invocation: gen_ai.system, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, gen_ai.response.finish_reasons, oya.foundry.capability, oya.tenant.id. The supervisor invokes capabilities (foundry.supervisor.spawn, foundry.supervisor.commit — §B.8) and spawns model-backed CLIs. SessionTicket carries model_hint and provider_family which map directly to gen_ai.request.model and gen_ai.system. SpendRecord carries tokens_in/tokens_out mapping to gen_ai.usage.input_tokens/output_tokens. None are emitted as span attributes.
findings.evidence: ADR-0042 §Per-capability gen_ai semantic conventions table; v4 §B.2.1 SessionTicket fields (model_hint, provider_family); v4 §B.2.1 SpendRecord fields (tokens_in, tokens_out); v4 §B.8 capability registry rows (6 capabilities declared).
findings.remediation: On the supervisor.driver.spawn span (F11-003 remediation), add: gen_ai.system = provider_family_to_gen_ai_system(ticket.provider_family), gen_ai.request.model = ticket.model_hint, oya.foundry.capability = 'foundry.supervisor.spawn'. On settle (commit), record gen_ai.usage.input_tokens = spend.tokens_in, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens = spend.tokens_out.

findings.title: account_id and model_hint cardinality risk undeclared
findings.description: AccountId(pub String) and model_hint: String appear in SessionTicket and SpendRecord. If either field is used as a metric label key, cardinality is unbounded: N accounts × M model hints = N×M label combinations. The plan declares N accounts as a design goal (multi-account fanout) and model_hint as a free-form string. VictoriaMetrics performance degrades sharply above ~1000 unique label combinations per metric.
findings.evidence: v4 §B.2.1 SessionTicket/SpendRecord field types; v4 §A.2 'multi-account-fanout' as decision driver #1; ADR-0042 'low-cardinality only per OTel conventions'; TelemetryMiddleware comment: 'Counter labels (low-cardinality only per OTel conventions)'.
findings.remediation: Define explicit cardinality policy in plan: (a) account_id MUST NOT appear as metric label — use provider_family (low-cardinality enum: 4 variants) instead. (b) model_hint in metrics MUST be normalized to a bounded enum (e.g., claude-3/claude-4/gpt-4o/gpt-5/gemini-pro/unknown) before use as label. Declare this policy in §B or a dedicated observability subsection.

findings.title: Health endpoint response content not specified — liveness is not observability
findings.description: GET /v1/supervisor/health is declared (v4 §B.7) but its response body is not specified. A health endpoint that returns 200 {} is not the same as one that returns {status: ok, in_flight: 2, inbox_depth: 5, last_tick_epoch_secs: 1747123456, loop_alive: true}. Without structured health content, external monitors cannot probe supervisor liveness, capacity saturation, or loop stall.
findings.evidence: v4 §B.7: 'route(HttpMethod::Get, "/v1/supervisor/health", handler_to_sync(HealthCheck))' — HealthCheck struct declared by name only, no response schema.
findings.remediation: Declare HealthCheck response schema: {status: 'ok'|'degraded', in_flight: u32, max_in_flight: u32, inbox_depth_estimate: u64, last_tick_epoch_secs: u64, accounts_eligible: u32, accounts_degraded: u32}. Wire to SupervisorApp state. This makes the health endpoint the primary 3am fast-path check before querying VictoriaMetrics.

findings.title: v5: Settings drift excluded accounts have no structured log or metric
findings.description: v5 §B.4 extends AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot() semantics: VerifyMode::FailOnDrift excludes drifting accounts from the returned Vec<ProviderAccount>. This silently reduces the account pool available to RoutePolicy::select. No log event is declared for exclusion, and no metric counts excluded accounts. On-call cannot tell from logs or metrics why fewer accounts are eligible.
findings.evidence: v5 §B.4: 'If VerifyMode::FailOnDrift and any account's DriftReport.entries contains a non-Match state, the account is excluded from the returned Vec<ProviderAccount>'; zero log or metric declaration in v5 §B.1..§B.9.
findings.remediation: In CompositeAccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot(): before returning, emit tracing::warn!(account_id_hash=%hash, provider_family=%pf, drifted_files=%n, 'supervisor.settings.account_excluded_drift') for each excluded account. Increment supervisor_settings_drift_total{provider_family, drift_state} counter.

findings.title: cron_loop / run_forever has no liveness heartbeat metric
findings.description: run_forever (v4 §B.2.5) is the tokio runtime host. If the async task loop stalls (e.g., tokio blocking pool exhausted, or inbox.peek_lock returns a Future that never resolves due to a broken async runtime), there is no observable heartbeat metric that monotonically increments to confirm the loop is alive. supervisor_quarantine_total could stay at 0 for two different reasons: (a) no poison messages (healthy), (b) loop is stalled (critical failure).
findings.evidence: v4 §B.2.5 run_forever declaration; v4 §B.3 'loop{sleep(1s)} fake-driver test' — this is a TEST construct, not a production heartbeat.
findings.remediation: Add a supervisor_loop_tick_total counter (no labels, monotonically increments every time the cron_loop fires). A flatline on this counter = loop stall = page. Cost: 1 counter increment per heartbeat_interval_secs (default from SupervisorConfig). Negligible overhead.

findings.title: v5: SettingsRenderer file I/O has no span — render/verify hangs are dark
findings.description: SettingsRenderer::render and SettingsRenderer::verify (v5 §B.2.2) perform filesystem I/O to ~/.claude/, ~/.codex/, ~/.gemini/. These are called inside AccountSnapshotProvider::snapshot() which is called at tick_once step 2. If render/verify is slow (NFS mount, quota exceeded, permissions), tick_once stalls. No span is declared around render or verify.
findings.evidence: v5 §B.2.2 SettingsRenderer trait; v5 §B.4 composition: 'snapshot() silently picks up the verify+render behavior'; zero span declarations in v5.
findings.remediation: Wrap each renderer call with tracing::span!(Level::DEBUG, 'supervisor.settings.verify', provider_family=%pf). Since Branch Y enforces zero new deps and tracing is already a workspace dep (Cargo.toml:481-492), this costs zero new dependencies.

summary.3am_diagnosability: FAIL — supervisor is not diagnosable from logs+metrics+traces alone. On-call requires SSH + manual JSONL inspection.
summary.adr_0042_conformance: PARTIAL — tracing crate is present (workspace dep confirmed); no OTel Meter, no span instruments, no gen_ai semconv attributes declared in plan.
summary.adr_0003_conformance: PARTIAL — audit_chain.rs test asserts EvidenceRef emission; emit_audit_event call does not conform to AuditEvent struct schema.
summary.critical_unknown: Whether the plan treats audit_chain.rs as the entire observability story (test-only) or whether a runtime OTel instrumentation layer is assumed to exist elsewhere and not declared here. If the former, blockers F11-001 and F11-003 require new grit units before execution. If the latter, the plan must cite the existing instrumentation crate and declare how supervisor-app hooks into it.
summary.discriminating_probe: Check whether oya-foundry-supervisor-app composes oya-observability-domain (found at crates/oya-observability-domain/src/lib.rs). If oya-observability-domain provides ObservabilityKit with tracer + meter + logger (per ADR-0042 §ObservabilityKit), then supervisor-app must declare its dependency on it in Cargo.toml and show the SupervisorApp::new() wiring. If this dependency is absent, all three BLOCKER findings (F11-001, F11-002, F11-003) require new plan sections before execution begins.
